key_insight: Multiscale simulations identify a dynamically stabilized hexagonal ZrO interlayer as a key driver of columnar oxide microstructure and a significant oxygen diffusion barrier during zirconium corrosion.
engineering_relevance: Predicting oxide morphology, oxygen transport, and local tensile stresses could help assess zirconium corrosion and crack initiation.
method: Compute ZrOₓ thermochemistry and material properties using density functional theory.
Use molecular dynamics with a DFT-trained machine-learned potential to supply additional model inputs.
Simulate oxide growth in MedeA PhaseField with heterogeneous nucleation, mass transport, and elastic effects.
evidence_signal: The simulations reproduce columnar oxide morphology and grain size distributions seen in micrographs, as well as an undulatory metal/oxide interface.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative validation metrics, and the proposed link between the ZrO barrier and sub-parabolic corrosion kinetics remains tentative.
paper_title: Multiscale Modeling of Zr Corrosion: Predicting Microstructures of Oxide Films
